completion_definition: Completed means the initial curated cross-reference pass: the source verse and every listed target passage were read in the pinned Saints-Translation English records, and each retained pair has a specific explanation. It does not mean every possible biblical connection has been exhausted, or independent scholarly approval.

review_receipts.reviewer_role: Personally read the actual complete source units and all selected target passages with necessary context, wrote each explanation, separately reread all 52 complete source/target/category/rationale triples, then reread seven refined complete triples. Pin checks are technical evidence only.

old_row.rationale: Solomon addresses Israel's commanders of thousands and hundreds, judges, and ancestral rulers. David's earlier assembly names those same classes of leaders; the comparison preserves the different kings and occasions.

new_row.rationale: The source lists Solomon's commanders of thousands and hundreds among Israel's leaders. David's earlier assembly includes commanders bearing those same numerical ranks and rulers over Israel; the different kings, occasions, and descriptions of other offices remain distinct.

changes.reason: Do not equate every differently described governing office.

old_row.rationale: Both describe Solomon offering a thousand whole burnt offerings on the altar at the high place. Chronicles specifies the bronze altar and tent setting; Kings describes the high place's prominence.

new_row.rationale: Both describe Solomon offering at the high-place altar with a stated thousand: Chronicles calls it a thousandfold whole burnt offering and Kings a thousand whole burnt offerings. The differing formulations are retained.

changes.reason: Preserve the source thousandfold formulation rather than replacing it with the target count wording.

old_row.rationale: Both describe Egyptian chariot and horse exports and onward trade for foreign kings, including Syria. Chronicles gives six hundred and one hundred fifty in silver; Kings gives one hundred and fifty respectively. The differing prices remain unreconciled.

new_row.rationale: Both describe Egyptian chariot and horse exports and onward trade for foreign kings, including Syria. Chronicles gives six hundred for a chariot and one hundred fifty for a horse; Kings gives one hundred for a chariot and fifty for a horse. The differing prices remain unreconciled.

changes.reason: Avoid ambiguity between a combined number and two separately stated prices.

old_row.rationale: Both replies bless God for giving David a discerning son to rule the people. Chronicles expands the blessing with creation language and Solomon's building purpose, while Kings reports Hiram's rejoicing at the message.

new_row.rationale: Both replies bless God for giving David a wise or discerning son. Chronicles expands the blessing with creation language and Solomon's building purpose, while Kings reports Hiram's rejoicing at the message.

changes.reason: Keep the shared blessing explicit without importing adjacent ruling language into this source unit.

old_row.rationale: Both name the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite as the place where the Lord responded to David. Chronicles' building notice locates the temple on that previously prepared site without requiring an equation of differently named sites elsewhere.

new_row.rationale: The source locates the building at Orna the Jebusite's threshing floor, where the Lord appeared to David. The target names that same floor as the place where the Lord answered David and David sacrificed; the shared site connects the accounts while their different verbs remain intact.

changes.reason: Distinguish appeared from answered while retaining the explicitly named site.

old_row.rationale: Both describe carved palm trees in the house's decoration. Chronicles places them with hanging ornaments on the paneled and gilded great house, while Kings specifies palm trees in the inner and outer rooms.

new_row.rationale: Both include palm trees in the house's decoration. Chronicles expressly describes carved palms on the paneled and gilded great house, while Kings lists palms in the inner and outer rooms after describing engraved cherubim.

changes.reason: Do not attribute an explicit carving verb to every object in the target sentence.

old_row.rationale: Both describe the two cherubim with their wings spread inside the house, spanning between the walls and touching in the middle. Chronicles additionally states their posture and orientation, which this target does not repeat.

new_row.rationale: The wings are spread across twenty cubits here. Kings describes spread wings reaching the two walls and meeting in the middle, the arrangement also detailed in Chronicles 3:11-12; only Chronicles here adds the standing posture and direction of the figures.

changes.reason: Distinguish the source unit from its necessary adjacent wing-arrangement context.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The source names Beseleel son of Ouriou son of Or, whereas Exodus names Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur. Their independent identity equation is not established by this supplied-English review. The completed pair concerns the explicitly located altar in 1 Chronicles 21:29, not this unverified name equation.

The craftsmanship accounts have differently written names and different maternal descriptions: Dan's daughters here, a widow's son from Naphtali in Kings. No reconciliation or personal identity equation is claimed. The retained same-chapter pair compares the request and the enumerated skills.

editorial_notes.note: The first three chapters were read after the complete 833-unit inventory. Retained comparisons preserve differences in office descriptions, thousandfold offering wording, chariots versus mares, trade prices, temple dimensions, pillar heights, and untranslated terms. The two proposed personal-identity equations remain unresolved and uncredited; retained connections use independently supported narrative, textual, material, or same-chapter evidence.

review_receipts.limitations: Initial supplied-English AI curation only; not exhaustive discovery, original-language or apparatus review, specialist approval, name-equivalence resolution, numerical reconciliation or live-anchor verification. Other 781 source units remain unread and pending. Inventory, extra context, pin checks and revisions earn zero review credit.

peer_review_receipts.reviewer_role: Independent of the author. Personally read all actual source units, complete retained target passages, categories, full rationales, necessary context, both unresolved proposals, and all seven before/after refinement triples in this turn. No reading or semantic approval is inherited from author flags.
peer_review_receipts.review_method: Fresh independent complete_text reads through show-triples.py in unclipped batches 1-18, 19-35, and 36-52, reading each actual source, full retained target, category and full rationale. Separately read all three complete source chapters with read-chapters.py, the listed necessary target contexts, and both unresolved candidate passages through passages.py. Finally rendered and personally read all seven exact original and seven exact replacement complete source/target/category/rationale triples through complete_text. Reviewed same-chapter links for substantive request/response, enumerated specifications, provision offer/acceptance, census assignment, or construction/installation antecedence. Preserved supplied names, roles, material quantities, measurements, and account differences.
peer_review_receipts.pin_method: Adapted check-pins-2-chronicles-1-3.py to a unique peer-independent prefix, then freshly fetched all five complete used-book raw files from the immutable commit. Verified each Git blob SHA1 against the source-check registry, computed SHA256, saved distinct peer raw artifacts, and compared each entire parsed cache with the fresh pinned data. Before freezing this receipt, independently rehashed saved raw artifacts, recomputed Git blob identities, and rechecked complete parsed-cache equality via pin_artifact_contract. Author files were untouched.

unresolved_candidates.reason: Personally read Beseleel son of Ouriou son of Or at the altar and Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur in Exodus 31:1-6. The supplied English names differ; this review does not independently resolve the proposed personal identity. The retained altar-location comparison with 1 Chronicles 21:29 is supported by the explicit tent and altar at Gabaon, without relying on the builder equation.

Personally read the Chiram description in 2:12-13 and Hiram in 1 Kings 7:1-2. Chronicles gives the mother from Dan's daughters; Kings gives a widow's son from Naphtali. The differently written names and family/tribal descriptions are preserved without reconciliation or an asserted personal identity. The retained comparison with 2:6 concerns specific requested and supplied craftsmanship skills and does not depend on that unresolved equation.

semantic_review_notes: All 52 actual source units have one retained supported pair. All 71 distinct retained target units were read in complete_text output. The five same-chapter links state meaningful request/response, specific skills, accepted provisions, census-and-assignment totals, and constructed/installed pillar relationships; none is a self-reference or a merely neighboring association.

Accept all seven author refinements: preserve different leader offices; thousandfold versus a thousand offerings; separate chariot and horse prices; the precise blessing rather than adjacent ruling language; appeared versus answered at the same named floor; the target palm wording; and the source-unit/context distinction for the wings.

The temple length remains sixty here and forty in the supplied Kings target, the pillars remain thirty-five versus eighteen, and the chariots/mares counts and categories remain distinct. The different chariot and horse prices, oil terminology, and source wood or gold details are not harmonized.

The actual supplied 1 Kings 7:36 names gold nails; 6:16-22 establishes the inner-sanctuary antecedent for 6:20; 6:1-1c establishes Solomon and the fourth year/second month; and 10:1-10 establishes the queen as speaker. The source numbering and actual continuation units were respected without substituting conventional verse-number assumptions.

The two proposed identity equations remain unresolved and receive no credit. Retained altar-setting and craftsmanship links stand on explicit independent textual correspondences. Untranslated ailam, serseroth, dabir, and source place/person spellings are not silently repaired or given unsupported equations.
peer_review_receipts.scope_limitations: Initial supplied-English AI semantic curation only. This is not exhaustive discovery, human specialist approval, original-language or apparatus review, numerical reconciliation, personal-identity resolution, or live-anchor verification. The 52 source units in chapters 1-3 were read; the other 781 2 Chronicles source units remain outside this semantic review. Inventory, extra context, technical checks, and refinements earn no additional completion credit.

acceptance.conditions: Acceptance binds these exact TSV and author-receipt bytes and the independently fetched pinned evidence. Later semantic changes require fresh review of complete changed triples and a new acceptance stage. Both identity proposals remain pending with zero source or pair credit.

source_verse.text: The bronze altar that Beseleel son of Ouriou son of Or had made was there before the Lord’s tent, and Solomon and the assembly sought it out.

target_verses.text: “Behold, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with a divine Spirit of wisdom, understanding, and knowledge in every kind of work,
to plan and design, to work in gold, silver, bronze, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen,
to work in stone and the woodworking crafts, and to perform every kind of work.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The craftsmanship accounts have differently written names and different maternal descriptions: Dan's daughters here, a widow's son from Naphtali in Kings. source_verse.text: his mother is from Dan’s daughters, and his father is a Tyrian man. He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and timber; to weave in purple, hyacinth blue, fine linen, and scarlet; to engrave engravings and devise every design, whatever you give him, with your skilled men and the skilled men of David my lord, your father.

target_verses.text: King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre,

a widow’s son, and he was from the tribe of Naphtali. His father was a Tyrian man, a bronze craftsman, filled with skill, understanding, and knowledge for doing every work in bronze. He was brought to King Solomon and did all the works.
